requirements.R1: Guest checkout sessions expire after 15 minutes of inactivity.
requirements.R2: A guest checkout session must never expire while the cart contains items.
requirements.R3: The checkout page shows the order total including tax before payment.

requirements.R1: A guest may place at most 3 orders per email address in any 30-day period.
requirements.R2: Each guest order receives a unique order number at confirmation.
requirements.R3: Guests may place any number of orders; no per-email order limit applies to guest checkout.

requirements.R1: Guest orders above 500.00 require an additional payment verification step.
requirements.R2: Every guest order, whatever its value, completes after a single payment step with no further verification.
requirements.R3: Payment is taken by card only.

requirements.R1: A guest can request deletion of their data by contacting support.
requirements.R2: Guest personal data, including name and email, is deleted 24 months after the guest's last order.
requirements.R3: Guest order records, including name and email, are retained for 7 years for audit purposes.

requirements.R1: A confirmation email is sent within 5 minutes of successful payment.
requirements.R2: The confirmation email shows the order number and the delivery address.
requirements.R3: Confirmation emails are sent once a day at 02:00 as a single batch.

note: R2 is an exception that narrows R1; both can be satisfied.

requirements.R1: A guest may place at most 3 orders per email address in any 30-day period.
requirements.R2: A shopper whose email matches a registered account is asked to log in and is not subject to the guest order limit.
requirements.R3: Each guest order receives a unique order number at confirmation.

note: R2 covers a case R1 is silent on; nothing contradicts.

requirements.R1: A confirmation email is sent within 5 minutes of successful payment.
requirements.R2: If the confirmation email bounces, the order remains valid and is not cancelled.
requirements.R3: The confirmation email shows the order number.

note: Different user types; both timeouts can hold at once.

requirements.R1: Sessions of registered users expire after 30 minutes of inactivity.
requirements.R2: Guest checkout sessions expire after 15 minutes of inactivity.
requirements.R3: An expired session returns the user to the start of checkout.

requirements.R1: A guest can track an order by following the link in the confirmation email.
requirements.R2: A guest can track an order by entering the order number and the email used at checkout.
requirements.R3: The tracking page shows the current order status and the expected delivery date.

requirements.R1: Tax is calculated on the delivery address.
requirements.R2: The cart total shown at payment equals the amount charged to the card.
requirements.R3: Guest and registered orders with the same cart and the same delivery address show the same totals.

requirements.R1: The guest details form has an optional, unticked marketing consent checkbox.
requirements.R2: Marketing email is sent to a guest only if they ticked the consent checkbox.
requirements.R3: Guests have no settings page, so consent is captured at checkout only.

note: An example in one requirement uses a state the rule in another requirement excludes.

requirements.R1: A refund is issued only for orders whose status is 'Delivered'.
requirements.R2: Refunds are paid back to the original payment method within 5 working days.
requirements.R3: A customer can request a refund from the order history page.
requirements.R4: Example: a customer cancels an order that is still 'Shipped'; the refund is issued the same day.

note: Clearing on a state the rule excludes is coherent: excluded orders carry no reminder.

requirements.R1: A payment reminder is raised on orders in status 'Pending' or 'Invoiced' once the due date has passed. Orders in status 'Draft' are excluded.
requirements.R2: A payment reminder is cleared when the order status changes to 'Paid', 'Cancelled' or 'Draft'.
requirements.R3: Reminders are evaluated every night at 01:00.

note: R4's example breaks both R3 (only Overdue shown) and R1 (Overdue needs 'In Progress'); either pair counts.

requirements.R1: A task is flagged 'Overdue' when its status is 'In Progress' and the current time is after its planned end.
requirements.R2: A task is flagged 'Late' when its status is 'Assigned' and the current time is after its planned start.
requirements.R3: If both conditions are true for a task, only 'Overdue' is shown.
requirements.R4: Example: a task planned 13:00-14:00 is still 'Assigned' at 14:10; the dashboard shows both 'Late' and 'Overdue' for it.

requirements.R1: Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery.
requirements.R2: Items marked 'final sale' are excluded from returns.
requirements.R3: A return is accepted for any non-final-sale item up to 20 days after delivery.

note: No shared words; the conflict follows from arithmetic.

requirements.R1: Stock levels are evaluated by a batch job that runs every 15 minutes.
requirements.R2: A low-stock alert is raised within 2 minutes of the stock level dropping below the threshold.
requirements.R3: The threshold is set per product by the warehouse manager.

note: No pair clashes alone; together an auto-applied discount plus a code breaks the no-stacking rule.

requirements.R1: Discounts cannot be combined on a single order.
requirements.R2: A loyalty discount of 5% is applied automatically to every order from a loyalty member.
requirements.R3: A loyalty member may enter promotion code SAVE10 on any order, to take 10% off.

requirements.R2: Passwords of service accounts do not expire; they are rotated by the key-management job every 180 days.
requirements.R3: A user is prompted to change an expired password at next login.

note: The example follows the rule exactly; easy to mistake for a contradiction.

requirements.R1: An invoice is flagged 'Overdue' when its status is 'Sent' and the current date is after its due date.
requirements.R2: Overdue evaluation runs every night at 01:00.
requirements.R3: Example: an invoice due on 5 May is still 'Sent' on 6 May; the 01:00 run on 6 May flags it 'Overdue'.
